title: Retrospec Sedona Zafu Meditation Cushion
blurb: A crescent zafu filled with buckwheat hulls, with a washable cotton cover and a carry handle. Sits you a little higher than the floor so the knees drop and the back stays upright.
note: The thing most people are missing when they say they cannot sit still is a cushion of the right height. A crescent shape gives the thighs somewhere to go, and buckwheat can be added or taken out until it is yours. It is the first thing we would put in a meditation corner.

title: Koshi Wind Chime, Terra tuning
blurb: A handmade chime from the French Pyrenees: eight tuned rods inside a bamboo resonator, in the Terra (earth) pentatonic tuning. Played by hand, or hung where there is a breeze.
note: This is the chime you hear at the start and end of most sound baths in Perth. Terra is the lowest and warmest of the four tunings, which makes it the one to begin with. It is a real instrument, and it is what practitioners actually carry.

title: JBM Cork Yoga Blocks, pair with strap
blurb: Two natural cork blocks and a cotton strap. Cork is heavier and grippier than foam, and does not squash over time.
note: Blocks bring the floor up to meet you, which is the difference between a pose you can hold and one you strain through. Two blocks and a strap is the whole kit a home practice needs, and cork is the material studios choose because it stays put.

title: Hugger Mugger Standard Yoga Bolster
blurb: A rectangular bolster with a firm core and a soft surface, handmade in the USA. The shape used in restorative and yin classes.
note: Restorative yoga is mostly the art of being held up by the right prop, and a bolster is the prop. Hugger Mugger's has been the studio standard for decades because the core does not go soft. Under the knees, along the spine, or across the lap for a long sit.

title: Amazon Basics High-Density Foam Roller, 30cm
blurb: A short, firm foam roller in moulded polypropylene. Small enough to keep beside the mat or take to class.
note: A roller does not need to be clever. It needs to be firm enough to hold its shape and short enough that you actually use it. This is the plain, inexpensive one, and the 30cm length is the right size for calves, thighs and the upper back without taking over the room.

title: Alaska Bear Silk Sleep Mask
blurb: A mulberry silk sleep mask with a contoured shape that keeps the fabric off the eyelids, and an adjustable strap.
note: The simplest change to an evening is making it dark. Silk sits lightly, does not pull at the skin, and this one is shaped so the eyes are not pressed. It is also the mask sound bath and yoga nidra hosts hand out, which is a fair recommendation on its own.

title: Dreamegg D1 White Noise Machine
blurb: A compact sound machine with 24 sounds, three auto-off timers, a dimmable night light and a headphone socket. Mains or USB powered.
note: Steady sound covers the uneven kind, and that is the whole trick. We chose this one for the timer, so it can play through the settling-in and switch itself off, and for a night light dim enough to be useful. It is also small enough to travel.

title: Breath: The New Science of a Lost Art
blurb: James Nestor's account of how we breathe and how we used to, drawing on breathing traditions, pulmonology and his own experiments. Paperback edition.
note: If a breathwork class has left you curious about why any of it works, this is the book to read next. It is a reporter's book rather than a manual, which is why it is so readable, and it sends most people back to class with better questions.

title: Wherever You Go, There You Are
blurb: Jon Kabat-Zinn's short chapters on mindfulness in everyday life, from the founder of mindfulness-based stress reduction. Paperback edition.
note: The one meditation book we would hand to someone who has never sat down to meditate. The chapters are two or three pages each, secular in tone, and you can open it anywhere. Thirty years on it is still the plainest introduction there is.

title: The 5-Minute Gratitude Journal
blurb: A guided journal with short daily prompts: a few lines in the morning, a few at night. Undated, so a missed day costs nothing.
note: A journal only works if it is short enough to keep doing. This one asks for five minutes and three lines, which is the amount most people will actually write, and undated pages mean no guilt about the gaps. A good gift because nobody buys it for themselves.
